title: Finite discrete condensed coefficients and ordinary module sheaves
statement: Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring with its discrete condensed structure $\underline A$, and let $T$ be a scheme. Work on the small pro-étale site with the size and sheafification conventions of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules] and [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor]. The pulled-back ring object $p_T^*\underline A$ is isomorphic, as a ring object, to the constant ring sheaf $A_T$. The section-action equivalence of [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence] gives an exact equivalence between internal $p_T^*\underline A$-module objects and ordinary $A_T$-module sheaves. Its termwise extension is an equivalence of unbounded derived categories preserving relative derived tensor products and every Tor-amplitude interval [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude]. It identifies the finite constant local models and bounded constructible finite-Tor subcategories of [sk-def-sfb-constructible], and preserves shifts, distinguished triangles, and small coproducts, hence their localizing closures [sk-def-localizing-closure]. For every scheme morphism $f:X\to Y$ and fixed compactification $X\xrightarrow{j}\bar X\xrightarrow{p}Y$ of $f$, these equivalences identify the module-object composite $Rp_*D(j_!)$ of [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-lower-shriek] with the ordinary constant-$A$ module-sheaf composite $Rp_*j_!$ for that same compactification [def-sfb-finite-derived-lower-shriek-compactification].

proof.text: The finite-discrete point and scheme comparisons give the canonical scalar-normalized ring isomorphism $c_T:A_T\cong p_T^*\underline A$. Compose section-action with restriction along $c_T$ to obtain $E_T$; the internal tensor and ring-isomorphism transport statements make it additive exact. The constant-ring equivalence gives $C_TE_T$ with fixed-$A$ coefficients.

source.place: Step 8, coefficient identification and exact derived equivalence between internal module objects and ordinary constant-ring sheaves.

proof.text: Descend $E_T$ and its inverse termwise; their units and counits descend. Compose the internal tensor and ring-isomorphism comparisons, and then the constant-scalar tensor comparison, on corresponding K-flat resolutions. This gives both coherent unbounded derived tensor comparisons. Exactness identifies cohomology; essential surjectivity on degree-zero sheaves matches every tensor test, preserving and reflecting each Tor interval.

source.place: Step 8, coefficient identification and exact derived equivalence between internal module objects and ordinary constant-ring sheaves.

proof.text: Transpose coefficient-sections compatibility to $c_Ub_h=\alpha_hh^{-1}c_T$. Apply the flat-ringed ordinary comparison with $R=A_T$, $S=(p_T^*\underline A)_{sec}$, $a=c$ and terminal index; ring isomorphisms give flatness. Compose with internal operation transport; restriction along $c$ carries its $j_{!,\rm sec}$ to a left adjoint $j_{!,R}$ of $j^*_R$. The constant-scalar geometric-adjunction lemma, with $b=b_h$, then gives the fixed-$A$ pullback/direct-image squares and the open-extension comparison, retaining units and counits. Its fixed-$A$ direct image is the pushforward of [def-sfb-finite-lower-star] (both are $G\mapsto G(-\times_TU)$ on underlying sheaves), and its supplied $j_{!,B}$ is the extension by zero of [def-sfb-finite-extension-by-zero], left adjoint to the restriction $j^*$ by [def-sfb-finite-extension-by-zero-adjunction].

proof.text: Apply the scalar-normalized constant-model lemma to $C_TE_T$: its regular-module comparison fixes each scalar, and step 3 supplies its localized comparisons. Thus the same covers and constructible strata give the same local models, also affine-locally on arbitrary schemes. Over finite $A$, a finite module has a finite free surjection with finite kernel, and a finitely presented module is finite. Cohomology and Tor comparison from step 2 now identify the bounded constructible finite-Tor classes.

source.place: Step 8, coefficient identification and exact derived equivalence between internal module objects and ordinary constant-ring sheaves.

proof.text: Equivalences preserve coproducts by their universal property. With shifts and triangles from step 2, both equivalences carry replete triangulated coproduct-closed subcategories to such subcategories. Step 4 identifies their generators. Intersecting gives both inclusions between localizing closures; this intersection definition works for any finite $A$.

proof.text: Apply the exact-equivalence derived-squares theorem to step 3 and the supplied unbounded pullback/pushforward derived pairs. Its right square gives $D(C_YE_Y)Rp_*\cong Rp_*D(C_{\bar X}E_{\bar X})$. Compose with the exact termwise open-extension comparison. The two specified compactification definitions identify the resulting functors with $Rp_*D(j_!)$ and $Rp_*j_!$ for the same $(j,p)$.

lean.statement: theorem moduleObject_ordinary_coefficient_equivalence [Finite A] [DiscreteTopology A] : ∃ E : ∀ T : Scheme.{u}, Encoding A T, (∀ T : Scheme.{u}, Nonempty ((E T).fixedDerived.functor.Monoidal) ∧ (∀ (K : DerivedCategory (Internal A T)) (a b : ℤ), a ≤ b → (DerivedCategory.torAmplitudeIn _ a b K ↔ Scheme.HasProEtaleTorAmplitude T A ((E T).ordinaryDerived.functor.obj K) a b)) ∧ (∀ (K : DerivedCategory (Internal A T)) (a b : ℤ), a ≤ b → (DerivedCategory.torAmplitudeIn _ a b K ↔ DerivedCategory.torAmplitudeIn _ a b ((E T).fixedDerived.functor.obj K))) ∧ (∀ M : Internal A T, HasFiniteConstantLocalModel (coefficient A) T M ↔ ordinaryLocalModel A T (((E T).ordinary.functor ⋙ (E T).fixed.functor).obj M)) ∧ (∀ K : DerivedCategory (Internal A T), (constantModelBoundedConstructible (coefficient A) T K ∧ DerivedCategory.finiteTorAmplitude _ K) ↔ ordinaryCtf A T ((E T).fixedDerived.functor.obj K)) ∧ Nonempty ((E T).fixedDerived.functor.CommShift ℤ) ∧ (E T).fixedDerived.functor.IsTriangulated ∧ PreservesColimitsOfSize.{u + 1, u + 1} (E T).fixedDerived.functor ∧ (∀ K : DerivedCategory (Internal A T), localizingClosureProEtale (coefficient A) T K ↔ CategoryTheory.localizingClosure (ordinaryCtf A T) ((E T).fixedDerived.functor.obj K))) ∧ (∀ (X Y : Scheme.{u}) (f : X ⟶ Y) (c : Compactification f), Nonempty (CondensedRing.rightDerivedLowerShriekOfCompactification (coefficient A) c ⋙ (E Y).fixedDerived.functor ≅ (E X).fixedDerived.functor ⋙ rightDerivedLowerShriekOfCompactification (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1} A)) c))
lean.note: The canonical coefficient map is sheafified constant functions followed by the existing constantSchemeIso and upperStarFromPoint. Encoding fixes the ring isomorphism on every constant scalar and fixes both forward functors to section-action/scalar restriction. Its two derived equivalences are the actual termwise Equivalence.mapDerivedCategory, not independent equivalences. Tensor and compactification comparison use the equivalent fixed-ULift-A module-sheaf presentation; Tor intervals are also compared directly with the recorded intrinsic HasProEtaleTorAmplitude. The ordinary local-model and constructibility helpers render the ordinary side of this node with the same covers, strata and affine-local convention; they introduce no new independent notion or chosen data. The two definition nodes def-sfb-constant-ring-module-restriction and def-sfb-constant-sheaf-scheme-pullback-comparison own the existing canonical constructions used by the signature; the associated theorem nodes are proof dependencies. The recorded derived-constant-module interface is also a statement dependency.
